title: Debt Crisis Heats Up: Higher Rates Could Break The System | Patrick Yip
speaker: Patrick Yip (APMEX / OneGold)

macro_themes.view: Federal debt above 100% of GDP means the Fed cannot sustain a Volcker-style hiking cycle, and a weaker dollar is the easy way out, which favors gold.
Central banks buying over 1,000 tons a year supports gold.
Silver mix, buybacks and refinery backlogs signalled the January peak; now metrics are back to normal with steady automated buying, so he doesn't see another big drop.
Gold is in a pause similar to the mid-1970s before a longer run, though cycles are getting smaller.

calls.reason: Debt above 100% of GDP, central bank buying, normalized retail sentiment with no selling, and portfolio math favoring a 20-30% allocation; within a year expects all-time highs or above.
calls.quote: sometime in the next year I wouldn't be surprised if we uh you know hit the all-time highs or even exceed that.

notes: No date in transcript; listing date used. Sponsored content (OneGold). Speaker had a $4,900 year-end target but backed away from it; long-term target 'all-time highs' left null because the ATH level was not stated (gold peaked above $5,000 in Jan 2026 per the interview). Medium-term bullish inferred from 'I don't think you necessarily have another big drop'. Says he sold silver at $103 in January; no current silver call.
